name: Clean Shave
shortLine: No hair on the face. Fresh and clean.
description: A smooth face with no beard. Fresh and clean.
pickIf: you want the cleanest, youngest look for any job.
skipIf: your skin gets red or bumpy after shaving.
daily: 5 min: shave, every day or every second day.
nextVisit: any time, for a hot-towel shave
suitsText: All face shapes · Any beard growth

faq.q: How do I avoid razor bumps?
faq.a: Shave with the hair growth, use a new blade and shaving cream, then rinse with cold water.

faq.q: How often should I shave?
faq.a: Every day or every second day for a smooth face.

faq.q: Is a barber shave better than shaving at home?
faq.a: A hot-towel barber shave is closer and gentler. It's a good choice before an event.

faq.q: Should the barber use a new blade?
faq.a: Yes, always. It's fine to ask.

barberSteps: Trim long hair first with trimmer.
Shaving cream. Shave with hair growth.

name: Light Stubble
shortLine: Very short, like 2–3 days of growth.
description: A very short beard, like 2–3 days of growth. Adds shape to the jaw but still looks clean.
pickIf: you want a little edge with almost no work. Works even with patchy growth.
skipIf: your job needs a clean shave.
weekly: Trim at home twice, trimmer at 1–2 mm.
nextVisit: in 2–3 weeks, to clean the lines
suitsText: All face shapes · Any beard growth

faq.q: What trimmer length is light stubble?
Does light stubble work with a patchy beard?
faq.a: Yes. At this length, gaps hardly show.

faq.q: How often should I trim it?
faq.a: Twice a week, to keep it at the same length.

faq.q: Does stubble need a neck line?
faq.a: Yes. A clean neck line keeps even short stubble neat.

barberSteps: Neck line: 2 fingers above Adam's apple.

name: Heavy Stubble
shortLine: Short and even, like one week of growth.
description: A short, even beard, like about one week of growth. Stronger than light stubble.
pickIf: you want a grown-up look without the care of a full beard.
weekly: Trim at home once, trimmer at 5 mm.
suitsText: All face shapes · Medium or full growth

faq.q: What trimmer length is heavy stubble?
faq.a: About 5 mm.

faq.q: What is the difference between light and heavy stubble?
faq.a: Light stubble is 1–2 mm, like 2–3 days of growth. Heavy stubble is about 5 mm, like a week.

faq.q: Will heavy stubble itch?
faq.a: It can in the first few days of growth. Beard oil helps.

faq.q: Is heavy stubble OK for office?
faq.a: Yes, if the cheek and neck lines are kept clean.

barberSteps: Cheek line: follow natural line. Clean.
Neck line: 2 fingers above Adam's apple.

name: Short Boxed Beard
shortLine: Short, neat beard with sharp cheek and neck lines.
description: A short, neat beard with sharp lines on the cheeks and neck. Well kept and professional.
pickIf: you want a beard that looks right in the office, or more shape for a round face.
daily: 1 min: a few drops of beard oil.
weekly: Trim at home once: 6 mm on the sides, 9 mm on the chin.
nextVisit: in 2 weeks, to sharpen the lines
suitsText: Oval, round, long and heart face · Medium or full growth

faq.q: What length is a short boxed beard?
faq.a: 6 mm on the sides and 9 mm on the chin.

faq.q: Why is it called a boxed beard?
faq.a: The sharp cheek and neck lines give it a square, boxed shape.

faq.q: Is a boxed beard good for a round face?
faq.a: Yes. The square corners add shape.

faq.q: How often should I trim it?
faq.a: Once a week at home. See the barber every 2 weeks to sharpen the lines.

barberSteps: Cheek line: straight and sharp. Razor.
Neck line: 2 fingers above Adam's apple.
Corners at jaw: square, not round.

name: Full Beard
shortLine: Thick, fuller beard, shaped and neat.
description: A thick, full beard, shaped round or square at the bottom. Strong and mature.
pickIf: your beard grows thick and you want a strong look.
skipIf: your growth is patchy or medium, or you have a long face.
suitsText: Oval, square and heart face · Full growth only

faq.q: How long does it take to grow a full beard?
faq.a: Usually 2–3 months, depending on how fast your beard grows.

faq.q: Do I need beard oil?
faq.a: Yes. It keeps the hair soft and stops the skin underneath getting dry and itchy.

faq.q: Round or square bottom: which is better?
faq.a: A round bottom softens a square face. A square bottom suits oval and heart faces. Ask your barber.

faq.q: How do I stop a full beard looking messy?
faq.a: Comb it every day and get it shaped every 3–4 weeks.

barberSteps: Cheek line: natural. Remove stray hair.
Neck line: 2 fingers above Adam's apple.

name: Goatee
shortLine: Hair on the chin only. Cheeks shaved.
description: Hair only on the chin, with the cheeks shaved.
pickIf: your cheeks don't grow much hair, or you want a round face to look longer.
weekly: Shave the cheeks 2–3 times. Trim the chin at 6 mm.
suitsText: Oval, round, square and heart face · Any growth, even patchy

faq.q: What is the difference between a goatee and a Van Dyke?
faq.a: A goatee is chin hair only. A Van Dyke adds a separate moustache and a pointed chin.

faq.q: Can I keep my moustache with a goatee?
faq.a: Yes. Pick a style in the Moustache slot, or choose a Van Dyke or Circle Beard.

faq.q: Is a goatee good for a patchy beard?
faq.a: Yes. It only needs hair on the chin.

faq.q: Does a goatee suit a round face?
faq.a: Yes. It makes the face look longer.

barberSteps: Chin: keep width of the mouth.

name: Van Dyke
shortLine: Pointed chin beard with a separate moustache. Cheeks shaved.
description: A pointed chin beard with a separate moustache and shaved cheeks. Classic, with character.
pickIf: your cheeks grow patchy but your chin and lip grow well.
daily: 1 min: comb the moustache, a little moustache wax if you like.
weekly: Shave the cheeks and the gap 2–3 times.
suitsText: Oval, round, square and heart face · Any growth, even patchy

faq.q: How is a Van Dyke different from a circle beard?
faq.a: A Van Dyke has a gap between the moustache and chin beard. A circle beard joins them.

faq.q: How long should the chin part be?
faq.a: 1–2 fingers, shaped to a point.

faq.q: Do I need moustache wax?
faq.a: It's not required, but a little wax helps the moustache keep its shape.

faq.q: Is a Van Dyke good for a patchy beard?
faq.a: Yes. It only uses the chin and upper lip.

barberSteps: Shave the gap between moustache and chin.

name: Circle Beard
shortLine: Moustache and chin beard joined in a circle. Cheeks shaved.
description: Moustache and chin beard joined in a circle around the mouth. Cheeks shaved.
pickIf: you want a neat, grown-up look but your cheeks grow thin.
skipIf: you have a very long face.
weekly: Shave the cheeks 2–3 times. Trim at 5 mm.
suitsText: Oval, round and square face · Any growth, even patchy

faq.q: What is a circle beard?
faq.a: A moustache joined to a chin beard in a round shape around the mouth.

faq.q: Is a circle beard the same as a goatee?
faq.a: No. A goatee is chin hair only. A circle beard includes the moustache.

faq.q: Is a circle beard OK for office?
faq.a: Yes. It looks neat and professional.

faq.q: How do I keep the shape round?
faq.a: Shave the cheeks 2–3 times a week, and get the outline sharpened every 3 weeks.

name: Chin Strap
shortLine: Thin line of beard along the jaw, ear to ear.
description: A thin line of beard along the jaw, ear to ear. Sharp and defined.
pickIf: you want a sharp jaw line.
skipIf: your beard grows patchy, or you can't shave often.
weekly: Shave above and below the line 3 times.
suitsText: Oval and round face · Medium or full growth

faq.q: How wide should a chin strap be?
faq.a: About 1 finger wide.

faq.q: Does a chin strap include a moustache?
faq.a: No, but you can add one in the Moustache slot.

faq.q: Is a chin strap hard to keep?
faq.a: Yes. The lines need shaving about 3 times a week.

faq.q: Does a chin strap suit a round face?
faq.a: Yes. It gives the jaw a sharper outline.

barberSteps: Follow the jaw bone, ear to ear.

name: Faded Beard
shortLine: Short at the top, fuller down the jaw. Goes well with a fade haircut.
description: The beard is short near the ears and fuller down the jaw. It blends into a fade haircut.
pickIf: you have a fade haircut and want hair and beard to match.
weekly: Trim at home once: 6 mm on the chin and jaw.
suitsText: Oval, square, round and heart face · Medium or full growth

faq.q: What is a faded beard?
faq.a: A beard that gets shorter near the ears and blends into a fade haircut.

faq.q: Do I need a fade haircut too?
faq.a: It looks best with one, so hair and beard flow together.

faq.q: How short is it at the top?
faq.a: About 1 mm at the sideburns, blending to 6 mm along the jaw.

faq.q: How often should I get it re-cut?
faq.a: Every 2–3 weeks, together with your haircut.

barberSteps: Match the hair fade at the sideburns.
Neck line: 2 fingers above Adam's apple.

name: Balbo
shortLine: Chin beard along the jaw with a separate moustache. No sideburns.
description: A short beard on the chin and lower jaw, with a separate moustache and no sideburns.
pickIf: you want a sharp, stylish beard that shapes a round or wide face.
skipIf: you have a long face, or your chin grows patchy.
daily: 1 min: beard oil, comb the moustache.
weekly: Shave the sideburns and gaps twice. Trim at 6 mm.
suitsText: Oval, round, square and heart face · Medium or full growth

faq.q: What is a Balbo beard?
faq.a: A beard on the chin and lower jaw, with a separate moustache and no sideburns.

faq.q: How is a Balbo different from a Van Dyke?
faq.a: A Balbo spreads wider along the jaw. A Van Dyke stays pointed at the chin.

faq.q: Does a Balbo suit a round face?
faq.a: Yes. It adds shape to a round or wide face.

faq.q: Is a Balbo hard to keep?
faq.a: Medium effort: shave the sideburns and gaps twice a week.

barberSteps: Keep beard on chin and lower jaw.
Moustache: trim above lip. Keep it separate.
Shave the gap at the mouth corners.
Neck line: 2 fingers above Adam's apple.

name: Anchor Beard
shortLine: Pointed chin beard with a thin moustache, shaped like an anchor.
description: A pointed chin beard that runs a little along the jaw, with a thin moustache. Shaped like an anchor.
pickIf: you want a sharp style that works with patchy cheeks.
skipIf: you have a long face, or no time to shave often.
weekly: Shave the cheeks 3 times. Trim the moustache at 3 mm.
suitsText: Oval, round, square and heart face · Any growth, even patchy

faq.q: Why is it called an anchor beard?
faq.a: Its pointed chin and jaw line look like a ship's anchor.

faq.q: How is it different from a Balbo?
faq.a: An anchor beard has a pointed chin and a thin moustache. A Balbo is wider along the jaw.

faq.q: Does an anchor beard work with a patchy beard?
faq.a: Yes. It only uses the chin, jaw and lip.

faq.q: How often do I need to shave around it?
faq.a: About 3 times a week.

barberSteps: Extend chin beard a little along the jaw.

name: Ducktail
shortLine: Full beard shaped to a point at the chin.
description: A full beard with short sides and a longer, pointed chin.
pickIf: you have thick growth and want a full beard with a different shape.
skipIf: you have a long face or patchy growth.
daily: 3 min: beard oil, comb into the point.
suitsText: Oval, round, square and heart face · Full growth only

faq.q: What is a ducktail beard?
faq.a: A full beard with short sides and a longer chin shaped to a point.

faq.q: How long does it take to grow?
faq.a: Usually about 3 months of full growth before it can be shaped.

faq.q: Does a ducktail suit a round face?
faq.a: Yes. The point makes the face look longer.

faq.q: How do I keep the point?
faq.a: Comb it down and into a point every day with a little beard oil.

barberSteps: Shape the chin to a point.
Neck line: 2 fingers above Adam's apple.

name: Long Beard
shortLine: Long, full beard, trimmed to keep a clean shape.
description: A long, natural beard grown well past the chin, with clean edges.
pickIf: you have thick growth and the patience to grow it long.
skipIf: you have a long face or patchy growth.
daily: 5 min: beard oil or balm, then comb.
suitsText: Oval, round, square and heart face · Full growth only

faq.q: How long does it take to grow a long beard?
faq.a: 6 months or more, depending on how fast your beard grows.

faq.q: Do I still need a barber while it grows?
faq.a: Yes. Shaping every 4 weeks keeps it looking cared for.

faq.q: How do I stop a long beard tangling?
faq.a: Comb it every day with beard oil or balm.

faq.q: Can I keep a long beard at work?
faq.a: Many jobs allow it if it's clean and shaped.

barberSteps: Ask: how much length to keep?
Comb beard down. Trim ends only.
Sides: shorter than the chin. Scissors.
Cheek line and neck line: clean.

name: Soul Patch
shortLine: Small patch of hair just under the lower lip.
description: A small patch of hair just under the lower lip. The rest of the face is shaved.
pickIf: you want a small, creative detail. Easy even with patchy growth.
daily: 3 min: shave around the patch, every day or every second day.

faq.q: What is a soul patch?
faq.a: A small patch of hair just below the lower lip.

faq.q: Can I add a moustache to a soul patch?
faq.a: Yes. Pick any style in the Moustache slot.

faq.q: Is a soul patch good for a patchy beard?
faq.a: Yes. It only needs a little growth under the lip.

faq.q: How big should the patch be?
faq.a: About 1 finger wide.

barberSteps: Shave the whole beard area clean.
Keep a small patch under the lower lip.

name: Mutton Chops
shortLine: Thick sideburns down to the jaw, with the chin shaved.
description: Thick sideburns down to the jaw, with the chin shaved. A bold, old-style look.
pickIf: you have a long face and want it to look wider.
skipIf: you have a round face or patchy cheek growth.
weekly: Shave the chin 2–3 times. Trim the sideburns at 6 mm.
suitsText: Oval and long face · Full growth only

faq.q: What are mutton chops?
faq.a: Thick sideburns that grow down to the jaw, with the chin shaved.

faq.q: Do mutton chops include a moustache?
faq.a: No. You can add one in the Moustache slot.

faq.q: Do mutton chops suit a round face?
faq.a: No. They make the face look wider.

faq.q: How do I keep them neat?
faq.a: Trim them at 6 mm every week and shave the chin 2–3 times a week.

barberSteps: Keep sideburns full, down to the jaw.
Shave chin and front of jaw clean.
